entry.title: ChatGPT vs. Logic: Why AI Code is Slower
entry.summary:
I recently set a simple task: Find the lowest value in a list and return all its indices. The rules were strict: Round 1: The ChatGPT Approach lst = [44,4,4,1,1,1,1,1,1,1,12,4,3,2,4,5,6,4,3,44,556,6,6,6,6,22,2,2,1]
# Step 1: Find lowest value manually lowest = lst[0] for num in lst: if num < lowest: lowest = num # Step 2: Find all indexes of lowest value result = {} indexes = [] for i in range(len(lst)): if lst[i] == lowest: indexes.append(i) result[lowest] = indexes print(result)
The Performance Cost: By being a bit more clever with our logic, we can achieve the same result in a single trip through the list.
lst = [44, 4, 4, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 12, 4, 3, 2, 4, 5, 6, 4, 3, 44, 556, 6, 6, 6, 6, 22, 2, 2, 1]
final_dict = {} temp = float("inf") for i, v in enumerate(lst): if v < temp: temp = v final_dict.clear() final_dict[v] = [i] elif v == temp: final_dict[v].append(i)
print(final_dict)
O(N) Complexity: It only loops through the list once. The "Short-Circuit" Effect: Once the code finds a 1, it ignores every other number that is higher (like 12, 44, or 556). It doesn't even enter the dictionary logic for those items. The 2026 Developer Verdict In the age of AI, it’s easy to settle for "code that works." But high-performance engineering is about looking at two loops and asking:"Can I do this in one?" What’s your take? Do you prioritize "Step-by-Step" readability, or do you always optimize for the single pass?
python #performance #algorithms #codingchallenge

entry.title: Running DBA: Why This Blog Exists
entry.summary: Hi, I’m Nuno, and welcome to Running DBA, a blog about SQL Server, automation, migrations, disaster recovery, and real-world DBA challenges. Let me be honest: I’m not an expert in any single area. What I do have is the skill to make things happen. I tackle problems as they appear, searching for solutions with determination and focus until they’re solved. That’s been my approach throughout my career, and it’s what keeps me learning every day. I’m what you could call a DBA by accident, and the person who got me into this world did it without mercy 😉. The best lesson I learned from him is that searching is a skill. Nobody knows everything, but what sets people apart is the willingness to learn. For most of my career, I was completely outside the SQL community. I worked in environments that weren’t always ideal, and I got used to it. It was my norm. Everyone has their challenges, of course. Joining DataMasterminds changed everything. Suddenly, I was part of a team where colleagues are not just highly skilled, but also genuinely care about each other. It’s like playing in the Champions League, with the bonus that everyone around you is extraordinary, both in knowledge and personality. I don’t know what tomorrow will bring, but this is by far the best place I’ve ever worked. On this blog, I’ll share what I learn daily: automating tasks, handling database migrations, designing disaster recovery plans, and mastering backups and restores. Expect practical tips, real-world examples, and stories from production, because theory is nice, but production is where the real lessons happen. Whether you’re a fellow DBA, a developer, or just curious about what it’s like to keep SQL Server running smoothly, this blog is for you. And yes, there will probably be some running metaphors along the way 😉
